title: Scenario
description:
What the persona came to do on this run. A scenario lives in scenarios/*.yaml and is versioned independently of persona cards, so a run is persona x scenario: the same person can be pointed at a different task without editing (and re-versioning) the card, and the same task can be given to several people without copying it into each card.

The persona says who; the scenario says what, where it starts, what counts as done, and what will happen to the session on the way. Its digest is bound into run.json at `pqa new-run` time and verified by the review gate, exactly like the persona card's.

target.description: The app this scenario is written for, matching run.json target.name. Omit for scenarios that apply to any app. Used by `pqa report` to decide which persona x scenario cells count as coverage gaps.

task.description: What the persona is trying to get done, in plain words. Re-injected alongside the persona summary, so write it the way the persona would say it, and keep it free of the persona's never_uses terms -- `pqa new-run` warns when it is not.

state.description: What is on screen at step 0, e.g. 'the basket, with one item in it'.

preconditions.description: State the operator establishes before step 1 (seed data, account, network). Not checked mechanically -- they describe the fixture, so that two runs of the same scenario start from the same place.

success_criteria.description: The completion test for the session. Must be externally observable -- something on screen or in the app's state, not 'the user is satisfied'. When a run has a scenario, these replace the persona card's success_criteria in run.json; the card's become the fallback for runs without one.

in_scope_surfaces.description: Surface prefixes this scenario covers. 'checkout' covers 'checkout/payment'. The gate warns when an observation lands outside them; the persona's out_of_scope list still applies on top.

perturbations.description: Interruptions decided in advance, in strictly increasing at_step order. Deciding them before the run is the same argument as the step budget (DESIGN.md section 3): an agent that chooses when to be interrupted chooses the moment least likely to hurt.
